analysis.summary: The PR introduces a functional isolation bug due to incorrect variable scoping and potential styling inconsistencies in the table component.

bugs.title: Module-scoped timer causes state conflicts across multiple tables
bugs.description: The 'scrollTimeout' variable is declared at the module level rather than within the component scope or a ref. If multiple Table components are rendered on the same page, scrolling one table will clear the debounce timer for all others.
bugs.risk: This causes incorrect UI behavior where the 'scrolling' state (used for visual indicators like sticky column shadows) fails to update or becomes stuck when users interact with different tables on the same page.

notBugs.reason: Using array index as keys for table cells and headers is acceptable here as the content is primarily read-only strings and the row structure is stable within its data source.
The early return for missing tabs occurs after all Hook declarations (useState, useEffect), so it does not violate the Rules of Hooks.
Defining 'TableComponent', 'HeadLine', etc., inside 'FlexibleTable' is a performance anti-pattern (causing remounts), but not a high-severity functional bug in a static comparison table.
